title: Straightening of left and right fibrations restricts space-valued transport
statement: Use quasicategories, Kan complexes, coherent functors, functor simplicial sets, cores and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left, right, Cartesian and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], space-valued transport of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], cocartesian straightening of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], the infinity category of small quasicategories of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure] and the opposite involution of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-opposite-involution]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and let $B$ be a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory. Let $i:\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ regard a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex as a quasicategory; for Kan complexes $K,L$ the simplicial set $\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)$ is Kan and equal to its core, so $i$ is a coherent fully faithful functor. (1) Every left fibration $p:E\to B$ is a cocartesian fibration, every edge of $E$ is $p$-cocartesian, and its fibers are Kan complexes. Hence every functor over $B$ between left fibrations preserves cocartesian edges, and the left fibrations with $\mathcal U$-small total space span a full subcategory $\operatorname{LFib}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{coCart}(B)$ whose mapping spaces are the Kan complexes $\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(E,E')$. (2) Write $T_B:\operatorname{LFib}(B)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ for space-valued transport and $\operatorname{St}_B$ for cocartesian straightening. There is a coherent natural equivalence $\operatorname{St}_B|_{\operatorname{LFib}(B)}\simeq i\circ T_B$ of functors $\operatorname{LFib}(B)\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U})$, whose component at $p$ evaluated at $b$ is equivalent to the identity of the fiber $E_b$. In particular a left fibration classified by $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ under space-valued transport is classified by $i\circ F$ as a cocartesian fibration. (3) Dually every right fibration $q:Y\to B$ is a Cartesian fibration all of whose edges are $q$-Cartesian. Define the Cartesian straightening of a Cartesian fibration $E\to B$ as $\mathrm{op}\circ\operatorname{St}_{B^{\mathrm{op}}}(E^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}):B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$. Then a right fibration classified by $X:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ under the right-fibration form of space-valued transport is classified by $i\circ X$ under Cartesian straightening, and the right fibrations form a full subcategory of the Cartesian fibrations on which this identification is a coherent natural equivalence. All these identifications are natural for maps of fibrations over $B$, including higher simplices, compatible with base change along maps $B'\to B$, and unchanged on enlarging $\mathcal U'$.
